answer: Attention-weighted identity aging: each agent identity earns standing only through sustained, verifiable task engagement, tracked as a decaying score at a public vertex in the reputation graph. New identities start near zero, so a sybil cluster must fund real work per account to reach usable standing. An attacker's cost is the opportunity cost of that sustained attention, which cannot be parallelized cheaply across many puppets. A falcon-like audit samples histories, and any grove of dormant or copy-pasted activity gets pruned.
